names: Stuart Lake Trailhead (Colchuck Lake trail, Eightmile Rd FR 7601)
Stuart Lake Trailhead (Colchuck Lake / Mountaineer Creek trailhead, Eightmile Rd)
landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest - Alpine Lakes Wilderness
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass
Northwest Forest Pass ($5/day or $30/annual) at the Stuart Lake Trailhead.
drive: From Leavenworth, drive US-2 west 0.8 mile, turn left onto Icicle Road for about 8.5 miles, then turn left onto Eightmile Road (FR-7600), stay right onto FR-7601 and follow it about 4 miles to the trailhead. The last stretch closes in winter, typically November to May.

Take I-90 Exit 38, turn right at the bottom of the ramp, and follow SE Homestead Valley Road around and under the I-90 overpass to the Dirty Harry's Peak trailhead (Far Side) lot. A Discover Pass is required.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Washington Pass Overlook, Blue Lake, and Cutthroat trailheads — $5/day or $30/annual (America the Beautiful pass also honored).
Northwest Forest Pass / Interagency Pass
drive: Drive SR 20 about 42 miles east from Newhalem, or about 31 miles west from Winthrop, to the Blue Lake trailhead on the south side of the highway just below Washington Pass; SR 20 is closed in winter.

landManager: U.S. Bureau of Reclamation land managed by WDFW (Banks Lake Unit, Columbia Basin Wildlife Area)
storedPass: A Discover Pass is required on WDFW lands, or a WDFW Vehicle Access Pass issued with a hunting or fishing licence.
drive: From Grand Coulee drive south on Highway 155, or from Coulee City drive north on it. Most of the frozen flows sit between mileposts 8 and 17, and you can pull off on the shoulder or in a pullout beside the one you want.

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Snoqualmie Ranger District) — Alpine Lakes Wilderness
storedPass: Alpental/Snow Lake Trailhead day-use fee: $5/day, or a Northwest Forest Pass ($30/yr) / America the Beautiful pass.
Northwest Forest Pass ($30/yr) or America the Beautiful pass, or a $5/day pass at developed trailheads.
drive: From the Alpental / Snow Lake Trailhead (~3,100 ft), at the end of Alpental Road off I-90 Exit 52, via the Source Lake fork

names: Cascade Pass Trailhead (end of Cascade River Road)
Cascade Pass trailhead (end of Cascade River Road)
landManager: National Park Service — North Cascades National Park, and USDA Forest Service — Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest
storedPass: None for day use; backcountry permit required for overnight trips
None for day climbing; a wilderness permit (not a parking pass) is only needed if bivying overnight.
drive: From Marblemount take Cascade River Road ~23 miles to its end at the Cascade Pass Trailhead

names: SR-20 Hairpin / Pond Pullout (east of Washington Pass)
SR-20 hairpin / pond pullout (east of Washington Pass)
landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Washington Pass Overlook, Blue Lake, and Cutthroat trailheads — $5/day or $30/annual (America the Beautiful pass also honored).
drive: From the hairpin-turn/pond pullout on SR-20 just east of Washington Pass (~5,100 ft), via the cairned climbers' paths

landManager: National Park Service — North Cascades National Park (Stephen Mather Wilderness)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass / Interagency pass at trailheads
Northwest Forest Pass at trailhead; North Cascades NP has no entrance fee
drive: From Bellingham, drive SR-542 east about 46 miles, which is 13 miles past Glacier, and just before the third crossing of the Nooksack River turn left onto FR-32, then follow it 5.3 miles to its end at Hannegan Campground, where the trailhead is.

names: Goodell Creek / Upper Goodell Group Camp trailhead (SR-20, Newhalem)
landManager: National Park Service — North Cascades National Park (Stephen Mather Wilderness)
storedPass: NPS wilderness permit (North Cascades NP has no general entrance fee).
No park entrance fee or pass is required — North Cascades NP is one of the few fee-free NPS units; only the backcountry camping permit above applies.
drive: From Burlington drive about 60 miles east on SR-20 to milepost 119 near Newhalem, where the steep, narrow dirt access road to the Upper Goodell group campground leaves the highway.

names: Eldorado Creek trailhead (Cascade River Road mile 20)
landManager: National Park Service — North Cascades National Park (Stephen Mather Wilderness)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass at the Eldorado Creek Trailhead
None — the Eldorado trailhead is inside North Cascades National Park, which charges no entrance fee and no trailhead parking fee.
drive: From Marblemount, go straight past the last gas station onto Cascade River Road, cross the bridge and drive to the Eldorado Creek trailhead at mile 20, on the right; the last 10 miles are gravel.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Methow Valley Ranger District (Pasayten Wilderness)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass
Northwest Forest Pass or WA Trail Park Pass
drive: From the Andrews Creek Trailhead (~3,040 ft) on West Chewuch Road / FR-51

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Darrington Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Mountain Loop Highway trailheads — $5/day or $30/year.
Northwest Forest Pass required at Mountain Loop Highway trailheads (e.g. Sunrise Mine TH for Vesper Peak) — $5/day or $30/year.
drive: From Granite Falls, take the Mountain Loop Highway east 11 miles to the Verlot Ranger Station, then continue 19.3 miles to the Barlow Pass Trailhead at the end of the pavement; the lot is on the left.

names: Esmeralda Basin Trailhead (North Fork Teanaway Rd)
landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Cle Elum Ranger District (Alpine Lakes Wilderness)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass ($30/yr) or America the Beautiful pass, or a $5/day pass at developed trailheads.
Esmeralda/Ingalls Way trailhead day-use fee: $5/vehicle/day or $30/year (Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency Pass).
drive: From I-90 exit 85 take SR-970 east 7 miles, turn left onto Teanaway Road, and after 7.1 miles bear right onto North Fork Teanaway Road. Where the pavement ends after 5.9 miles take the right fork onto FR-9737 and continue about 9.5 miles, keeping left at the Beverly Campground fork and right at the fork for the trailhead, to the parking area.

names: Dingford Creek Trailhead (Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road)
landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Snoqualmie Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass ($30/yr) or America the Beautiful pass, or a $5/day pass at developed trailheads.
Northwest Forest Pass required at Salmon La Sac, Pete Lake, and Necklace Valley trailheads — $5/day or $30/year.
drive: From I-90 exit 34 near North Bend, follow 468th to Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road, turn right and drive 12 miles, passing the large Middle Fork parking area on the right. Cross the large concrete bridge, immediately turn right onto the gravel road signed for Dingford and Dutch Miller Gap, and follow it about 6 miles to the gate and trailhead.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest — Pasayten Wilderness
storedPass: None needed at the Ross Dam trailhead.
No day-use pass needed at the Ross Dam Trailhead; overnight wilderness permit required for camping.
drive: From Newhalem, drive SR-20 east about 14 miles; the trailhead parking is on the right between mileposts 134 and 135.

names: Downey Creek Trailhead (Trail #768, Suiattle River Road)
landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Darrington Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Downey Creek Trailhead — $5/day or $30/year.
Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful Pass required at the trailhead
drive: From Darrington, drive Highway 530 to the Suiattle River Road (Forest Road 26) and turn east; the trailhead is in a parking lot just past the Downey Creek bridge, about 20 miles from Highway 530. Since November 5, 2026 the road has been closed to vehicles at milepost 12, so the last 8 miles must be covered on foot or by bike.

names: Boston Basin climbers' trailhead (Cascade River Road)
landManager: National Park Service — North Cascades National Park (Stephen Mather Wilderness)
storedPass: None — there are no trailhead or parking fees for trails that begin on National Park Service land, and there is no fee to enter the North Cascades National Park Service Complex.
None at the Boston Basin trailhead — it is inside North Cascades National Park, which charges no entrance fee, and parking at the Cascade River Road pullouts is free.
drive: From Seattle, drive I-5 north to Burlington, then WA-20 east through Marblemount, and turn onto Cascade River Road, following its paved-then-gravel surface about 21.7 miles to a small pullout at 3,200 ft that marks the unmaintained Boston Basin Trailhead (a different stop from the Eldorado trailhead about 2.5 miles down-road, and just before the road's end at Cascade Pass).

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest — Alpine Lakes Wilderness
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass / Interagency Pass or day-use fee
Northwest Forest Pass ($30/yr) or America the Beautiful pass, or a $5/day pass at developed trailheads.
drive: From the Pete Lake Trailhead off FR-4616 near Cooper Lake (~2,850 ft), via Pete Lake Trail #1323 and the Chimney Creek climbers' path

landManager: Olympic National Park (summit, Home Lake and the Home Creek basin); Olympic National Forest — Hood Canal/Quilcene Ranger District, Buckhorn Wilderness — for the Upper Dungeness Trail approach
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass, Interagency Recreation Pass or Digital Pass displayed at the Upper Dungeness Trailhead

Northwest Forest Pass, Interagency Pass or Scan & Pay at the Upper Dungeness Trailhead — $5 per vehicle per day or $30 annual. The trailhead is on Olympic National Forest land (Quilcene Ranger District), so no Olympic National Park entrance fee is charged to park there.
drive: From US-101 near Sequim Bay State Park, turn onto Louella Road, then Palo Alto Road, which becomes FR-28 at the forest boundary; turn right onto FR-2880, stay left onto FR-2870, and continue to the trailhead parking just past the Dungeness River bridge.

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Darrington Ranger District); the peak and much of the approach lie within or adjacent to WA DNR's Morning Star Natural Resources Conservation Area, not Glacier Peak Wilderness.
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Mountain Loop Highway trailheads (e.g. Sunrise Mine TH for Vesper Peak) — $5/day or $30/year.
Northwest Forest Pass / America the Beautiful Pass
drive: From the Sunrise Mine Trailhead (~2,340 ft) at the end of FR-4065 off the Mountain Loop Highway, via Trail #707

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Washington Pass Overlook, Blue Lake, and Cutthroat trailheads — $5/day or $30/annual (America the Beautiful pass also honored).
drive: From Washington Pass, drive SR-20 east past the hairpin turn to the next major pullout, near milepost 166; park there.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Wenatchee River Ranger District; upper trail and summit are within the Glacier Peak Wilderness boundary.
storedPass: None (no Northwest Forest Pass or fee is required at this trailhead).
Northwest Forest Pass ($5/day or $30/annual) required to park at the Phelps Creek and Trinity trailheads; not required for the Holden Village/ferry approach
drive: From US-2 at Coles Corner take SR-207 north, then Chiwawa River Road (FR-62) about 22 miles and Phelps Creek Road (FR-6211) about 2.3 miles to the Phelps Creek Trailhead. Chiwawa River Road is closed to vehicles north of the Atkinson Flats Campground junction by a storm-damage order from May 20, 2026 through December 31, 2027, unless lifted sooner, so the trailhead cannot be reached by car; check the road status before you go.

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mt. Baker Ranger District) — Mount Baker Wilderness, with some upper routes crossing into North Cascades National Park
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at most trailheads — $30/year or $5/day.
Northwest Forest Pass (or interagency day-use pass)
drive: From Mount Baker Highway (SR-542) about 1 mile past the Glacier Public Service Center, turn right onto Glacier Creek Road (FR-39), follow it about 8 miles, then turn left at the junction and go less than half a mile to the trailhead.

names: North Touchet Road roadside (The Dikes, below Ski Bluewood)
landManager: Umatilla National Forest (Walla Walla Ranger District)
storedPass: No -- informal roadside pullout, not a developed fee site
drive: From Dayton via North Touchet Road toward Ski Bluewood (paved ~15-16 miles, then gravel FR); Megadike South crosses the road about 1.2 miles above the Middle Point Ridge trailhead — roadside parking at the crags

landManager: National Park Service
storedPass: Not a Northwest Forest Pass (that's a USFS pass and doesn't apply inside the park). Standard NPS entrance fee applies: $30/vehicle (7 consecutive days), $55 Mount Rainier annual pass, or $80 America the Beautiful interagency annual pass.
America the Beautiful pass or $30/vehicle entrance pass
drive: From the Paradise parking lot

names: Excelsior Campground road pullout (Mount Baker Highway milepost 40)
drive: Drive east on the Mount Baker Highway (SR 542) to milepost 40 and park off the pavement on the old road to the closed Excelsior Campground and pump house.

landManager: North Cascades National Park (everything beyond Easy Pass) / USDA Forest Service — Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (trailhead to Easy Pass)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass ($30/yr) or America the Beautiful pass, or a $5/day pass at developed trailheads.
Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful/Interagency Pass required to park at the Easy Pass trailhead (day-use fee otherwise applies).
drive: From Marblemount, drive SR-20 east about 45 miles and turn right between mileposts 151 and 152 onto the signed Easy Pass road to the trailhead.
Take I-90 Exit 38 and follow SE Homestead Valley Road to Forest Service Road 9020, just before the road passes under I-90. Drive about 0.2 miles up FS 9020 to a pullout on the right.

names: Trinity Trailhead (end of Chiwawa River Road)
landManager: Glacier Peak Wilderness, Wenatchee River Ranger District, Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass or National Forest Day Pass required for Trinity Trailhead parking ($5/day or $30 annual); Interagency/America the Beautiful and National Park passes also honored.
Northwest Forest Pass required at some trailheads (fee day-use sites) — $5/day or $30/year.
drive: From US-2 at Coles Corner, turn north on SR 207 and go about 4.4 miles, turn right onto Chiwawa Loop Road, then take the second left onto Chiwawa River Road (Forest Road 6200). Follow it about 23 miles to the Trinity Trailhead; it turns to gravel at about 11 miles and the last stretch is very rough.

names: Lincoln Park lot on Southeast Blvd
drive: From Perry Street heading south, turn left onto 18th, which becomes Southeast Boulevard. The small, poorly signed lot is in the trees on the left about 0.5 miles along.
